PullRequest.Title: sessions: polish cloud automations
PullRequest.Body:
Fixes microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog#10292, microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog#10293, microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog#10320, microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog#10346, microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog#10347

## Why

Cloud Automations had five low-risk UX gaps discovered in testing: unsupported actions were exposed, repository ownership guidance did not recover the draft, shared automations used internal terminology, and history trigger metadata disappeared on interaction.

<details>
<summary>Code stats and validation</summary>

- 11 files changed, 173 insertions, 37 deletions
- Focused browser suites: 394 passing
- Adjacent Automations browser suites: 317 passing
- `npm run typecheck-client`: passed
- Targeted ESLint: passed
- `git diff --check`: passed
- Signed-in Agents Code OSS: 5/5 scenarios passed
- Changed-line coverage: unavailable; coverage-mode tests completed but emitted no usable changed-line report

</details>

## Changes

- Hide **Duplicate** for event-triggered automations (microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog#10292).
- Rename repository-owned grouping to **Shared automations** while preserving its description (microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog#10293).
- Explain private-repository ownership support and restore only ownership to **Only me** after rejection (microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog#10320).
- Hide **Export** for cloud automations while retaining it for local automations (microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog#10346).
- Keep run-history trigger labels visible on pointer hover, synthetic hover, keyboard focus, and in accessible output (microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog#10347).

## Verification

- Added regression coverage for action gating, ownership grouping and recovery, provider error translation, hover/focus styling, and accessible help/output.
- Verified all five behaviors in the signed-in Agents window using the shared Code OSS profile.
- Blast-radius analysis remained within Automations; the provider-neutral rejection type is the only shared workbench contract change.

Scenarios.Scenario: Render and refresh the Automations catalogue, then open a card's More Actions menu
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The catalogue autorun synchronously groups all automations, updates persistent card DOM, computes the new cloud/event context keys, and returns; the menu later reads those scoped keys. No subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, or network operation is on this changed path.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: The number of visible automation descriptors; each refresh visits each descriptor once, and the added event check scans that descriptor's small trigger-name record. Persistent cards avoid reconstruction on warm refreshes.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single synchronous renderer on the UI thread; no queued or parallel boundary work is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cards and scoped context-key services are retained by automation ID and reused across refreshes. Context-key writes suppress change events when values are unchanged. There is no new positive or negative remote cache.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the O(number of automations plus trigger names) path and in the absence of an expensive boundary; surrounding render and context-key implementations were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Very large catalogues could increase linear UI work, but the diff adds only two bounded boolean context updates and one small trigger-name scan per card; no evidence establishes meaningful latency or jank.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The added action gating is bounded per card, reuses persistent cards, and does not introduce layout reads, allocation growth, or boundary fan-out.

Scenarios.Scenario: Hover or keyboard-focus an automation run-history row with an external trigger label
Scenarios.CriticalPath: CSS selector matching changes the existing badge from hidden back to flex for the active row; browser style/layout/paint is the only work before the label appears.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One interacted row at a time in the virtualized session list; selector matching is scoped beneath the Automations history run list.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous browser style recalculation for the interaction; no application queue or asynchronous work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The existing badge DOM is reused. No data cache, request, or reconstruction is added.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that the change is CSS-only and reaches no IPC, filesystem, network, or subprocess boundary.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact style/layout duration depends on DOM size, but the selector is scoped and affects an already-rendered, fixed-height badge in the interacted row.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The rule does not create unbounded layout work or per-frame script and preserves fixed row height.

Scenarios.Scenario: Select Repository ownership, submit a cloud automation to an unsupported repository, then explicitly retry after the dialog resets ownership to Only me
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each Save waits for draft synchronization/customization state, resolves the repository, then the existing provider mutation performs repository manageability validation and the GitHub create request. After the first request rejects, the changed code only updates the two-option radio, warning, and validation state before returning control; a second boundary sequence occurs only if the user explicitly clicks Save again.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve a local workspace's GitHub repository from Git configuration when the target is a local file URI.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most once per explicit Save attempt for a local workspace; direct github-remote targets require no filesystem resolution.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same repository resolution ran before every create attempt.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must complete before the provider can submit the mutation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request per explicit mutation attempt; mutations are serialized globally for this store.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same configuration request preceded creates before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks the create request and dialog completion.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Submit the GitHub cloud automation create mutation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request per explicit Save; a user-triggered retry adds one request exactly as it did after a manual ownership change before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same create request was issued; unsupported ownership previously surfaced a generic Error and left Repository selected.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The dialog remains in committing state until the request succeeds or rejects.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist the repository in profile machine storage before create.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One storage write per explicit create attempt, serialized with the mutation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same profile-storage update occurred before each create attempt.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs synchronously before the network create operation.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One selected automation draft and one repository per user Save action. A rejection plus explicit retry produces two serialized mutation attempts, the same effective cardinality as manually changing ownership and retrying before the diff.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The dialog guards against concurrent saves, and GitHub mutations run through a provider-wide Sequencer. Cold target eligibility checks elsewhere are limited to five, but this save path remains serialized.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The GitHub API client is coalesced by clientPromise and reused warm. Target eligibility/privacy/manageability have caches, although mutation validation still performs its existing configuration request. Customization reload is a no-op because ownership does not change the target key. Unsupported ownership is not negatively cached, but the diff does not automatically retry it.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from tracing dialog commit through ProviderAutomationService, CloudAutomationStore, and GitHubCloudAutomationStore, including the Sequencer and client cache.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Network and local Git-config latency vary, but their call count, sequencing, and critical-path placement are unchanged by the typed error and local ownership reset.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The diff neither adds an automatic retry nor increases boundary cardinality; recovery adds only bounded local UI updates on a rare rejection.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open accessibility help or accessible Automations output after ownership terminology changes
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Localized strings are assembled synchronously; accessible output iterates the already-loaded automation collection and formats existing fields. No external operation is required.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Linear in the already-loaded automation and run collections, unchanged by the label edits.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single synchronous string-building pass; no background tasks or fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Uses current in-memory observables and templates; no new cache or retained state.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that no changed boundary, allocation scaling, or scheduling mechanism was introduced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Collection size controls existing output construction cost, but the diff changes only string contents.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Terminology-only changes preserve the pre-diff work and cardinality.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 11 changed files and traced catalogue rendering, interaction styling, dialog recovery, provider mutation boundaries, caches, and concurrency. No high-confidence diff-introduced performance regression was found.
